Author: Jim Thomas
Title: GRADUATION LOSSES LEAVE SAINTS THIN
Summary: Jim Thomas' 2004 Savannah Morning News preview introduced Bob Curley's first St. Andrew's football season as a rebuilding year after the Saints graduated 13 starters from the 2003 playoff team.
SourceCitation: Jim Thomas, "GRADUATION LOSSES LEAVE SAINTS THIN," Savannah Morning News (GA), August 20, 2004, Page 8N, Section: PREP FOOTBALL 2004.
Transcript:
GRADUATION LOSSES LEAVE SAINTS THIN

Bob Curley faces a rebuilding season in his first year as head coach at St. Andrew's after replacing Kevin Kunst.

Thirteen starters graduated from last year's 5-4-1 team that lost in the first round of the SCISA playoffs. The only returning starters are senior running back/linebacker Matt Knight, senior offensive lineman/defensive end David Stubbs and junior center/linebacker Jamie Cooper.

"That leaves us pretty thin and inexperienced," said Curley, who coached the middle school team last year. "But I think we'll still make the playoffs. There're only five teams in the region and the top three go. If you win two games, you're pretty much assured of going to the playoffs."

For the Saints to make the playoffs, though, Curley will have to count on contributions from eight or nine freshmen.

Another key is finding a quarterback to run the multiple offense the Saints will employ. Russell DeMasi, the son of Groves coach Karl DeMasi, was scheduled to be the starter, but he decided to go to Savannah Christian after spring practice. The top candidates to replace DeMasi are Knight and sophomores Jess Howard, Justin Redmond and Trevor Shanklin.

"I'm going to have to dig back in the old playbook," said Curley, who was an offensive lineman under Pepper Rodgers at Georgia Tech from 1973-77. "I didn't see any strong passing in spring practice. We're looking for someone who can handle the ball decent. But four weeks of spring practice doesn't tell you much."

Source: Savannah Morning News (GA), August 20, 2004, Page 8N, Section: PREP FOOTBALL 2004. By Jim Thomas.

Author: Noell Barnidge
Title: ST. ANDREW'S SAINTS - SAINTS PLAYERS ARE MARCHING FOR A VICTORY
Summary: A Savannah Morning News preview of Bob Curley's second St. Andrew's football season, including preseason expectations, key returning players, and the published roster.
SourceCitation: Noell Barnidge, "ST. ANDREW'S SAINTS - SAINTS PLAYERS ARE MARCHING FOR A VICTORY," Savannah Morning News (GA), August 19, 2005, Page 11, Section: HIGH SCHOOL FOOTBALL 2005.
Transcript:
ST. ANDREW'S SAINTS - SAINTS PLAYERS ARE MARCHING FOR A VICTORY

Despite being winless and outscored by 362 points last season, the St. Andrew's football team, is optimistic about this season.

The Saints, 0-10 last season, scored 21 points. They gave up 383.

But they aren't giving up on the coming season.

"We will definitely improve over last season," St. Andrew's second-year head coach Bob Curley said. "Every positive is a 100 percent improvement over last year."

This season, St. Andrew's plays the same 10 teams in the exact order in which it played them last season. With a more creative Pro-Set offense, Curley anticipates the Saints will not be held scoreless until the ninth game of the season, as they were last season.

"We're real young this year, but we were even younger last year," said Curley, who has three seniors and a junior among his 22 players. "I don't have much maturity, but I have some size."

Four players are over 200 pounds. The size of linemen Jamie Cooper (6-foot-1, 230 pounds), Ben Oliver (6-3, 260), Adam Fox (6-1, 210), and Tim Svoboda (5-7, 205) should benefit St. Andrew's.

Conditioning also will determine St. Andrew's success, as Curley plans to have most of his players playing on offense and defense.

"Particularly the older fellas," he said. "I just got through telling them that they better be prepared to play about 80 plays."

St. Andrew's three seniors - Cooper, Frank Howard (5-7, 160, RB-DE) and Garrett McCarthy (5-10, 165, RB-LB) - are being counted on to provide leadership.

Curley said Frank Howard and junior Jeff Howard (5-10, 165, RB-DB) will get the bulk of the carries at running back. In the passing game, sophomore wide receiver Patrick Maleki (6-3, 180) will be the primary target.

"This year, we'll have a better corps of skill position players," Curley said. "We haven't gotten into the defensive side of the ball yet (as of Aug. 4). We only started practice on Monday, so we haven't had a chance to fine-tune anything on defense."

Three players are competing for the starting job at quarterback. Sophomore Bubby Pavlo (5-9, 125), the backup last season to team co-captain Matt Knight, who graduated, is being given "a long, hard look" by the Saints' coaching staff. Pavlo is competing for the job with two freshmen, Jon Hope (5-10, 155) and Jim Kingston (5-9, 130).

St. Andrew's smallest margin of defeat last season was a 6-0 loss to Memorial Day in a non-league game. This season, St. Andrew's will be the visitor when the teams play Aug. 26.

In South Carolina Independent School Association 3-AA competition, St. Andrew's lost to Hilton Head Christian (42-0), Hilton Head Prep (40-0), First Baptist Church of Charleston, (49-0) and Colleton Prep Academy (48-14) in four consecutive weeks.

This season, Curley said, "We expect to be competitive in our region."

Author: Sean Coughlin
Title: EX-SCPS FOOTBALL COACH MILLER RETURNS TO COACH ST. ANDREW'S
Summary: A Savannah Morning News report on St. Andrew's hiring former Savannah Christian coach Jack Miller to revive the football program before the 2006 season.
SourceCitation: Sean Coughlin, "EX-SCPS FOOTBALL COACH MILLER RETURNS TO COACH ST. ANDREW'S," Savannah Morning News (GA), February 3, 2006, Page 6D, Section: SPORTS.
Transcript:
EX-SCPS FOOTBALL COACH MILLER RETURNS TO COACH ST. ANDREW'S

Retirement didn't suit Jack Miller, and neither did the golf, fishing, crabbing and traveling that went with it.

So earlier this week the 75-year-old went back to what he knows best: coaching.

St. Andrew's School announced Thursday that it has hired the Savannah coaching icon to try and revive its struggling football program.

The Saints, a member of the South Carolina Independent School Association, have gone a combined 1-19 the past two seasons.

Bob Curley, the program's head coach the past two seasons, will be one of Miller's assistants.

"I did not like retirement, and I wasn't in a position to help any young people or be a mentor to anybody," said Miller, who retired as Savannah Christian's head coach in Nov. 2004 after a nine-year stint. "I feel like I was put here to help people, and that's what I'm going to do again. I look forward to working with the St. Andrew's school and community."

Miller, a Tybee Island resident, said he received a call earlier this week from E.C. Hubbard Jr., headmaster at St. Andrew's, a private school on Wilmington Island. By "Tuesday or Wednesday" he accepted the job.

"After I looked at the school," Miller said, "I thought it was a very nice place. I felt like I had something to offer it. They asked me if I could help them for a few years. We're gonna work hard at it and see if we can't get the program where the administration wants it."

Miller, a member of the Greater Savannah Athletic Hall of Fame, has a 50-year coaching career, 30 as a head football coach, 20 as an assistant. He won 153 games during his career, which included stops at Vidalia (1961) Screven County (1962-63), Groves (1966-68), Clarkston (1971-76), Rockdale County (1977), Southwest DeKalb (1981-82) and Savannah Christian (1996-2004).

His last team, the 2004 Red Raiders, went 9-2, reaching the Georgia High School Association Class AA playoffs.

Miller was named the Georgia Athletic Coaches Association Football Coach of the Year three times - 1962 at Screven Co., 1973 at Clarkston and 1981 at Southwest DeKalb.

Miller, a graduate of Savannah High and Alabama's Troy State (now called Troy University), has also been a head coach in boys' basketball, boys' and girls' tennis, boys' golf and boys' and girls' track and field. He has more than 700 combined victories as a head coach.

Miller said he met with St. Andrew's players Thursday. He plans on holding spring practice in the coming weeks.

Author: Victor Fernandes
Title: Football Coach Leaves St. Andrew's After Five Years
Subtitle: David Boylston resigned after five seasons to take the Pinewood Prep job.
Summary: Boylston left St. Andrew's after a 41-17 five-year run that included the 1998 SCISA Class AA title and three straight championship-game appearances.
SourceCitation: Victor Fernandes, "FOOTBALL COACH LEAVES ST. ANDREW'S AFTER FIVE YEARS," Savannah Morning News (GA), December 7, 1999, Page 5D.
ArchiveNote: This archive page preserves citation details and an original summary. The full newspaper text is not republished here.
Transcript: The archive summary records David Boylston's resignation to become Pinewood Prep's head coach and business manager. The article summarized his St. Andrew's tenure as 41-17 with two runner-up finishes, the 1998 state championship and a 1999 first-round playoff berth.
